title: Calendar type picker empty on first boot
description: Settings -> Content -> Calendar Sources has a Type select populated from /api/plugins?plugin_type=calendar, but the frontend filters out plugin types where p.enabled === false. Built-in plugin types are registered in PluginTypeDB with enabled=false by default, so a fresh install can show an empty calendar type picker even though built-in calendar plugin classes (google, proton, ical) are available.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh install shows Google Calendar, Proton Calendar, and iCal Feed in the calendar type picker. Type picker options represent available plugin types, not enabled instances. Adding a calendar source works without requiring a separate plugin-type enable toggle first.

title: Dashboard admin dropdown can be blocked by empty photo overlay
description: On the dashboard, the settings/admin overflow dropdown can appear behind or be blocked by the 'No images available' photo placeholder/region overlay. Dashboard.vue currently raises .dashboard-stage/.dashboard-main above clock bars for focus-glow rendering, while the admin overflow menu z-index is only local to the clock bar. Result: the dropdown is visible/partially visible but not clickable in some empty-photo layouts.
acceptance_criteria: Admin overflow trigger and menu remain clickable above dashboard regions and empty photo placeholders in top, bottom, left, and right clock-bar positions. Existing focused-region glow behavior is preserved as much as possible.

title: Built-in themes missing from packaged runtime
description: The backend expects built-in themes at backend/data/themes/builtin.json or /app/data/themes/builtin.json. The file is missing from the repo/runtime image, so startup logs: Built-in themes file not found ... using empty themes. Result: built-in theme selection can be empty or incomplete on a fresh Docker/Unraid install.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh Docker image includes built-in themes at a path loaded by app.api.routes.plugins.themes. /api/plugins?plugin_type=theme returns built-in themes without warnings. Theme detail endpoint returns variables/dark_mode for each built-in theme.

title: Perimeter focus-light progress comet on clock-bar seam
description: Ambient loading indicator: a focus-light comet orbits the content-area perimeter (the rectangle the clock bars frame) while Calvin is refreshing. Rail = .dashboard-stage rect, so the light runs along a clock bar's own seam where a bar exists and the screen/region edge elsewhere. Calm now (indeterminate lap tied to backgroundRefreshing), playful-ready (config flag + event hook stubbed). Retires the clock-refresh-icon spinner. Respects prefers-reduced-motion.
close_reason: Closed

title: Zip path traversal in plugin & theme install (arbitrary file write / RCE)
description:
The subdirectory-extraction branch of both installers writes zip members to disk with NO path-containment check, allowing a crafted zip to escape the target dir and overwrite arbitrary files.

backend/app/services/plugin_installer.py ~lines 210-227: when plugin.json lives under a subdir in the zip, the loop does target_path = member[len(prefix):]; target = plugin_path / target_path; open(target,'wb'). A member named 'myplugin/../../../evil.py' strips to '../../../evil.py' and the OS follows the '..' at write time. backend/app/services/theme_installer.py ~lines 244-260 has the identical loop; note ThemeInstaller already HAS a correct _is_safe_path() (resolve().is_relative_to()) but only calls it in enumerate/install_from_repo, never in the zip extraction loop.

The extractall() branch (manifest at zip root) is NOT vulnerable — Python 3.12 extractall() sanitizes traversal. package_validator.validate_zip_structure only inspects manifest content, not member names, so it does not catch this.
design: Verified REAL, high confidence, with an EXECUTED repro in scratchpad (Python 3.12.13): zip members ['myplugin/plugin.json','myplugin/plugin.py','myplugin/../evil_plugin.txt'] -> evil_plugin.txt landed at plugins/evil_plugin.txt, OUTSIDE plugins/myplugin. Theme installer identical. plugins_dir defaults to backend/data/plugins; '../../../..' reaches backend/ and can overwrite app/main.py etc. -> arbitrary code execution on next restart/reload. The POST /api/plugins/install endpoint has no auth Depends; Calvin is a LAN self-hosted device but anyone who can reach the HTTP port can trigger it. Fix suggestion in acceptance.
acceptance_criteria: Both extraction loops reject any member that resolves outside the target dir (reuse ThemeInstaller._is_safe_path / add target.resolve().is_relative_to(base.resolve()) guard). Add a security test that feeds a zip with a '../' member and asserts the install is rejected and no file lands outside the plugin/theme dir.
close_reason: Both zip-extraction loops now reject members resolving outside the target dir (plugin_installer._is_within; theme_installer reuses _is_safe_path). Raises ValueError; partial dir cleaned up. Security tests added for both (../ member rejected, nothing escapes).

title: Event system misattributes handler results when a subscriber is rate-limited
description:
backend/app/services/event_system.py builds the per-handler task list by SKIPPING rate-limited handlers, but then pairs the gathered results against the FULL, unfiltered handler list. When any subscriber is rate-limited, len(results) < len(handlers) and the zip() at ~line 183 (_process_handler_results) misaligns: a result gets attributed to the wrong plugin and trailing plugins get no result at all. The same structural error exists in the fire-and-forget path (~lines 102-105, _await_handlers_with_error_handling).

Data flow: emit() (~53-62) iterates handlers and 'continue's past rate-limited ones, so tasks only covers non-skipped handlers; asyncio.gather (~69) yields results 1:1 with TASKS; but _process_handler_results(results, handlers) is passed the full handlers list; inside, 'for result, (plugin_id, _) in zip(results, handlers)' pairs results[0] (first non-skipped handler) with handlers[0] (which may be the skipped one).
design: Verified REAL (high confidence) by adversarial refuter. Repro: subscribe plugin A and B to event 'foo'; emit twice in quick succession so A is rate-limited on the 2nd emit; tasks=[task_B], results=[result_B], but zip([result_B],[(A,hA),(B,hB)]) -> processed['A']=result_B and B is dropped. wait_for_handlers=True callers receive a dict with wrong plugin_id keys and missing entries; fire-and-forget path logs errors under the wrong plugin_id. Fix: build results against the SAME filtered handler subset used to create tasks (carry (plugin_id, handler) alongside each task), not the original list.
acceptance_criteria: Results/errors are keyed to the correct plugin even when some handlers are rate-limited; add a unit test with 2 subscribers where one is rate-limited on the second emit.
close_reason: emit_event now tracks task_plugins aligned 1:1 with the created (non-rate-limited) tasks; both result processors zip against that instead of the full handlers list. Unit test added: A rate-limited, B's result stays keyed to B and isn't dropped.

title: Global UI-size setting: token scale + ui/ primitive tokenization
description: Add a global user-configurable UI size (Compact/Default/Large/Extra-large) driven by a --ui-scale multiplier. Introduces the sizing token layer (--space-*/--fs-*/--radius-*/--touch-target/--control-height/--toggle-*) in theme.css, tokenizes the ui/ control primitives, adds the uiSize config field + useUiScale composable + Settings control. Foundation that unblocks calvin-bvw. Vocab doc: docs/design/2026-07-04-ui-sizing-tokens.md. Plan: ~/.claude/plans/i-d-like-a-global-twinkly-eclipse.md
notes: Closing: implementation commit f9aa9b0 is merged into develop (verified via git merge-base --is-ancestor). Code was already green — 893 frontend unit tests + 11 backend config tests (uiSize round-trip + registry-parity guard), eslint + vite build clean. Remaining item was live visual QA across presets; user confirmed the work is in develop and opted to close without the separate QA pass. Reopen if a preset regression surfaces (Default pixel-identity, RegionControls cluster, FOUC on reload).
close_reason: Closed

title: Hot-corner reveal: long-press gesture, drop 'off', size + hold-time sliders
description:
Follow-up to calvin-hgy (PR #61). Three changes:

1. LONG-PRESS REVEAL (occlusion fix): the 64px corner currently intercepts short taps meant for calendar/photo content underneath. Make the corner visual pointer-events:none (pure hint, keeps keyboard <button>), and detect a configurable long-press by coordinates at the dashboard level (reuse the startRegionResize pointerdown pattern). Short taps fall through to content; press-and-hold in the corner reveals. Suppress the trailing content click via a time-bounded capture-phase listener.

2. DROP 'off': remove the 'off' option from Reveal corner. Opacity 0 already gives invisible-but-active. Persisted 'off' normalizes to bottom-left (removes the lockout footgun).

3. SLIDERS: add hotCornerSize (clamped slider, px) and hotCornerLongPressMs (clamped slider, ms) settings under Display -> Kiosk & touch. New reusable ui/RangeSlider.vue.

Store: config.js + configRegistry.js (hotCornerSize default 64, hotCornerLongPressMs default 500). Overlay: MinimalUIOverlay.vue. Gesture: new composable + Dashboard.vue wiring. Settings: DisplaySettings.vue. Tests + Playwright touch verification.
close_reason: Long-press reveal (occlusion fix): MinimalUIOverlay is now pointer-events:none; press-and-hold in the corner reveals via new useHotCornerReveal composable (window-level pointerdown + coordinate hit-box, reusing the startRegionResize pattern), suppressing the trailing content click. Short taps fall through to calendar/content. Dropped 'off' (normalizes to bottom-left, kills the lockout footgun; opacity 0 = invisible-but-armed). Added hotCornerSize + hotCornerLongPressMs sliders (new ui/RangeSlider.vue) under Display -> Kiosk & touch. 775 unit tests pass, eslint+prettier clean, build clean. Playwright-verified in the running app: short press keeps UI hidden, long press reveals; hold-time threshold honored (500ms<900ms no reveal, 1000ms reveals); opacity-0 corner still reveals.

title: FIX: breadcrumb/section indicator updates unreliable across categories
description: Reported 2026-06-29. The E3 topbar section indicator (scroll-spy via IntersectionObserver in Settings.vue) updates unreliably on all categories. Likely root cause: the observer uses the VIEWPORT as root with rootMargin '0px 0px -70% 0px', but after the E3 sticky app-shell the sections scroll inside .settings-content (which starts ~150px below the viewport top, under the fixed topbar+search). The detection band no longer aligns with the content pane, so the 'topmost visible section' pick is flaky (last section may never reach the band; updates lag/skip). Proper fix: set observer root to the .settings-content scroll container and tune rootMargin relative to it (or compute the active section from scrollTop). Use systematic-debugging; verify on-device across Plugins/Content/Device/Maintenance.
close_reason: Fixed on feat/design-settings-cycle-c (a4dc497..b39d0b8). Root causes: scroll-spy matched .settings-section (incl. embedded CollapsibleSections without eyebrows) and short trailing sections couldn't reach a top reference line. Now keys off .settings-section__eyebrow with midpoint activation + at-bottom clamp; observer→scroll-position compute rooted at .settings-content. On-device verified across Content (4/4 sections) and Maintenance (3/3). 704 tests.

title: Display-agent applies per-kiosk device-physical config (orientation/brightness/output)
description: The per-kiosk override store (dd9.3) serves device-physical values (orientation/orientationFlipped/applyDisplayRotation, and future brightness/output/resolution) in the effective config, and deviceConfigVersion bumps on change. What's missing: the device-side display-agent (deploy/kiosk-agent/calvin_display_agent.py) must READ those from GET /api/kiosks/<id>/config, apply via xrandr/backlight, and honor the CALVIN_DISPLAY_ROTATION env escape hatch as the winning layer (device-local > per-kiosk > global). Use the version-poll/ETag (dd9.3) to detect changes. This is the deferred 'agent-apply' slice; merges with dd9.1 (brightness/resolution/output).
acceptance_criteria: A per-kiosk orientation set via PUT /api/kiosks/<id>/overrides is applied on that kiosk by the display-agent (xrandr) within the poll interval; CALVIN_DISPLAY_ROTATION env overrides it; no server changes needed.
close_reason: merged to develop

title: Decide where 'orientation' lives: global server config vs device-local/per-kiosk
description: The global server config currently holds orientation=landscape/orientationFlipped, applied by the backend's display_orientation_service at startup. In server+kiosk this is wrong: orientation is physical per-Pi, but the setting is global. Decide the canonical home.
design: Options: (a) move orientation entirely to device-local (/etc/default/calvin-kiosk), drop it from server config; (b) keep in server config but make it per-kiosk (Tier 2); (c) keep global as a default, allow device-local override (precedence: device-local > per-kiosk > global). Tier-1 rotation this session uses device-local, so at minimum device-local must win. Also decide fate of display_orientation_service (backend-local, dead weight in Mode B) and the Settings UI orientation control.
acceptance_criteria: A documented decision on orientation's canonical location + precedence, and follow-up issues to migrate the config/UI/service accordingly.
close_reason: merged to develop

title: Multi-screen: one Pi driving multiple outputs mapped to separate content
description: Support a single Pi with multiple physical outputs, each mapped to its own dashboard/content (the 'separate screens to separate kiosks' idea).
design: Hardest / furthest out. Needs: multiple Chromium instances or windows pinned per xrandr output; per-output content assignment (extends per-kiosk assignment to per-output); device-local settings become per-output (rotation/resolution per output). May reframe 'kiosk identity' as per-output identity. Likely revisit after single-output per-kiosk works.
acceptance_criteria: One Pi shows different dashboards on different physical outputs, each independently configured.

title: Per-kiosk content assignment: map dashboards/regions to specific kiosks
description: Assign which dashboard / regions / view a given kiosk shows, so different kiosks display different content from one server.
design: Builds on kiosk-identity + per-kiosk config. A kiosk resolves its assigned dashboard/regions from its per-kiosk config. Relates to the existing regions/mode system (useModeStore, LayoutManager). Consider a 'kiosk profile' concept grouping a set of assignments reusable across kiosks.
acceptance_criteria: Two kiosks pointed at the same server can show different assigned content, configured from the UI.
close_reason: merged to develop

title: Kiosk identity: each Pi announces a stable id to the server (keystone)
description: Introduce a stable per-kiosk identity so the server can distinguish kiosks. This is the keystone for all Tier-2 per-kiosk features (per-kiosk config, dashboard assignment, multi-screen).
design: Store CALVIN_KIOSK_ID in /etc/default/calvin-kiosk (default derivable from hostname/MAC on first setup-kiosk.sh run). Kiosk sends it to the server: as a query param (?kiosk=<id>) and/or header on /api/config and data requests, and the Chromium URL could carry it. Server records seen kiosks (id, last-seen, hostname) so the UI can list/manage them. Keep backward-compatible: no id => current global behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A kiosk has a stable id, sends it with requests, and the server records/lists known kiosks. No behavior change for kiosks without an id.
close_reason: merged to develop

title: Server-side per-kiosk config store + merged /api/config
description: Let the server hold per-kiosk overrides layered over the global config, and serve the merged result to each kiosk based on its identity.
design: Depends on kiosk-identity. Storage: per-kiosk config rows keyed by kiosk id (overrides only). /api/config?kiosk=<id> returns global config deep-merged with that kiosk's overrides. Settings UI gains a per-kiosk view to edit overrides. Decide precedence + which keys are override-able. Note interaction with configRegistry (frontend) and config_service (backend).
acceptance_criteria: A kiosk-specific override (e.g. a different display schedule or dashboard) is served only to that kiosk; kiosks without overrides get global config unchanged.
close_reason: merged to develop

title: Tier 1: device-local display settings via /etc/default/calvin-kiosk + display-agent
description: Device-physical settings live on the Pi in /etc/default/calvin-kiosk and are applied locally by the display-agent (deploy/kiosk-agent/calvin_display_agent.py) on startup. First instance: screen ROTATION (implemented this session — CALVIN_DISPLAY_ROTATION applied via xrandr on agent startup). This issue tracks generalizing the pattern to other device-physical settings: brightness/backlight, resolution/mode, and which HDMI output is primary.
design: Env keys in /etc/default/calvin-kiosk (e.g. CALVIN_DISPLAY_ROTATION, CALVIN_DISPLAY_OUTPUT, CALVIN_DISPLAY_BRIGHTNESS). Agent applies them once at startup before the schedule loop, via xrandr (rotation/mode/output) and the backlight sysfs or ddcutil (brightness). setup-kiosk.sh should scaffold sensible defaults + document the keys. Mirrors backend display_orientation_service semantics (landscape->normal, portrait->left, flipped->inverted).
acceptance_criteria: Rotation works device-locally and survives reboot (done); pattern documented so brightness/resolution/output can be added by extending the env file + agent, no server changes.
notes:
Rotation implemented in display-agent (apply_rotation via CALVIN_DISPLAY_ROTATION, xrandr, startup one-shot) + tests + docs. Committed on develop. Remaining under this issue: brightness, resolution, primary-output selection. Live-apply on the existing Pi still pending (needs xrandr output name + desired orientation).
Live-applied on the existing kiosk (calvin@calvin): CALVIN_DISPLAY_ROTATION=left on HDMI-1, log shows 'rotation applied: HDMI-1 -> left'. Rotation slice DONE; issue stays open for brightness/resolution/output follow-ups.

title: Per-device (per-kiosk) settings model for server+kiosk deployments
description:
As Calvin shifts from all-in-one Pis to a central server + multiple dumb kiosks (Mode B, see docs/setup/DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGIES.md), settings that are physical to a specific Pi, or that assign different content to different kiosks, no longer fit the single GLOBAL server config. This epic defines the per-device settings model.

## Context
Trigger: after converting a Pi from all-in-one to remote kiosk (backend on server at calvin.wholab.xyz), two regressions surfaced that are both instances of the same gap — the local backend used to apply device-physical operations (screen power schedule, screen ROTATION) via local xrandr/vcgencmd, and a remote backend cannot. Screen scheduling was solved with a device-local display-agent (deploy/kiosk-agent/calvin_display_agent.py) that reads the schedule from /api/config and applies it locally. Rotation is being solved the same way (Tier 1, device-local env). This epic covers the BROADER model beyond those point fixes.
design: Two tiers. TIER 1 — device-physical settings (rotation, brightness, resolution, which HDMI output): belong ON the Pi, in /etc/default/calvin-kiosk (device-local), applied by the display-agent. No server changes. Rotation is the first instance (see child). TIER 2 — per-kiosk server-side config (which dashboard/region/screen each kiosk shows; multi-screen mapping): needs a KIOSK IDENTITY (each Pi announces a stable id) and server config keyed by that identity. Keystone = kiosk identity; everything else builds on it. Open question: does 'orientation' stay in global server config (currently orientation=landscape there, wrong for multi-kiosk) or move to device-local/per-kiosk? Current display_orientation_service + display_power_service both assume backend-is-local (main.py lifespan) — Mode B breaks that assumption generally; document which display ops are backend-local and thus need a device-side path.
acceptance_criteria: A documented, implemented model where: device-physical settings are configured per-Pi and applied locally; each kiosk has a stable identity; the server can serve per-kiosk config; and a kiosk can be assigned specific content/screens. Delivered incrementally via the child issues.

title: Calendar sources duplicated between Content tab and plugin settings
description: Calendar sources are plugin instances. They are managed in two places: the dedicated Content -> Calendar Sources tab and the generic Plugins calendar plugin cards/instance modals. Both surfaces can add/edit/delete/toggle the same sources, and InstanceModal also contains calendar-specific color/show-time fields. This creates duplicate settings paths and unclear ownership.
acceptance_criteria: Decide the canonical calendar-source management surface. Either remove/hide the duplicate generic calendar instance controls, or narrow the dedicated tab to source-specific display controls, or clearly cross-link the two. Color, show-time, enabled, ordering, add/edit/delete, and refresh behavior each have one obvious owner.

title: Clarify first-boot enabled semantics for built-in plugin types
description: We need to decide whether built-in plugin types should be marked enabled=true on first boot, or whether plugin-type enabled should only mean globally active/visible while instance creation remains available regardless. The current backend registers built-in types disabled by default, but the UX expectation is that built-in calendar plugins are 'on' and usable on first boot.
acceptance_criteria: Document and implement the chosen semantics. Fresh first boot exposes built-in calendar source types. Plugin management UI language distinguishes plugin type availability from individual source/instance enabled state.

title: Remove legacy RegionControls floating cluster — consolidate touch controls onto the region header rail
description:
## Summary
The floating touch control cluster `RegionControls.vue` (‹ prev / › next / ↻ refresh / ⤢ fullscreen) is a PRE-#83 legacy control set. PR #83 (calvin-6ig) moved region controls onto the header rail but never removed this cluster, so when a region is FOCUSED + isTouch it renders a second, redundant set of controls. Confirmed on real device (user screenshots) for calendar and service regions. Detection fix (calvin-c37, PR #86) means this now also shows on Auto once a touchscreen is correctly detected.

## Root cause (verified this session)
`RegionControls.vue` renders `v-if="isTouch"` and is placed in each region view's `#actions` header slot `v-if="focused"`:
- CalendarView.vue:32, WebServiceViewer.vue:29 & :49, PhotoSlideshow.vue:26.
- `focused = lightActive && id === activeRegionId`; `lightActive` is false when the layout is UNLOCKED (Dashboard.vue:391), so this is NOT an unlock bug — it triggers on normal focus/selection while isTouch.
- Its actions map to keyboard actions (calendar_prev/next/refresh/enter_fullscreen; web_service_prev/next, service_refresh, web_service_enter_fullscreen; images_prev/next, photos_enter_fullscreen).

Per-region overlap with the header rail:
- CALENDAR: `.calendar-header` ALWAYS shows Previous ‹ / Next › / Fullscreen ⤢ (NOT isTouch-gated) → the floating cluster's ‹ › ⤢ are literal DUPLICATES. Unique in the cluster: ↻ refresh (calendar has no header refresh).
- SERVICE: WebServiceViewer header nav (‹ ›) + fullscreen (⤢) are gated `v-if="!isTouch"`, so on touch the floating cluster is currently the ONLY nav. Header shows ServiceRegionViewOptions (tune) on touch. Unique in cluster: ↻ service_refresh.
- PHOTOS: PhotoSlideshow relies on the floating cluster as its only touch control set (verify whether it has any header rail at all).

## Goal
Header rail is the SINGLE control set on touch too; delete the floating `RegionControls` cluster without losing any function per region kind.

## Proposed approach (DESIGN FIRST — user asked to brainstorm/plan before implementing)
- Calendar: drop the dup; decide whether to add a ↻ refresh button to `.calendar-header` (calendar auto-refreshes on interval, so refresh may be optional) — design call.
- Service: remove `!isTouch` gate on the header nav/fullscreen so they show on touch; add a ↻ refresh (service_refresh) to the header. Keep ServiceRegionViewOptions.
- Photos: PhotoSlideshow needs header controls on touch (prev/next/fullscreen) since it currently only has the floating cluster — give it a header rail consistent with calendar/service.
- Then delete `RegionControls.vue` and its imports/usages; keep the keyboard-action wiring (handleAction) intact for keyboard users.
- Confirm header controls still size with 'Dashboard size' (regionChromeVars: --icon-size/--icon-font) and IconButton size=custom (see PR #83 fullscreen-fallback fix commit 9638662).

## Files
- Delete/retire: frontend/src/components/dashboard/RegionControls.vue (+ tests: tests/unit/components/dashboard/RegionControls.spec.js)
- Edit: frontend/src/components/CalendarView.vue, frontend/src/components/WebServiceViewer.vue, frontend/src/components/PhotoSlideshow.vue
- Check: frontend/src/composables/useKeyboardActions.js (keyboard actions must remain reachable)

## Acceptance criteria
- With isTouch true and a region focused, NO floating ‹ › ↻ ⤢ cluster appears; only the header rail controls.
- Calendar: single row of controls (no duplicate ‹ › ⤢).
- Service: header shows nav + fullscreen + refresh + view-options on touch; can navigate/refresh/fullscreen/scroll (card-grid) with touch.
- Photos: prev/next/fullscreen available on touch via header.
- Keyboard actions (calendar_prev/next, web_service_*, images_*) still work.
- Controls scale with Dashboard size; no fullscreen-header regression.
- Verify live on the docker dev stack (Playwright) across calendar + service + photos with touchControls=on.

## Context / provenance
- Sibling to calvin-c37 (touch detection). Detection half shipped: PR #86 (fix/touch-detection-maxtouchpoints).
- Depends on nothing; independent of the merged card-grid work (PR #85, calvin-fub Part B) but that's what exposed it (touch users need the card-grid scroll, which needs isTouch true).
close_reason: Consolidated region controls onto header rail behind hasPointer; deleted RegionControls; uniform hidden-unless-selected; merged to develop 7bafcdb

title: Touch detection misses touchscreens (Auto) + isTouch+unlocked legacy-controls bug
description: Surfaced during calvin-fub Part B verification. (1) useTouchCapability 'auto' gates isTouch on matchMedia('(any-pointer: coarse)') only — misses touchscreens that report as mouse / hybrid Pi panels; add navigator.maxTouchPoints>0 (and 'ontouchstart' in window) to the auto heuristic. (2) touchControls is the ONLY input to isTouch; when isTouch=true AND layout unlocked (!regionsLocked), an extra set of legacy controls renders (user report). Fix the duplication. Both bugs block touchscreen users from the card-grid scroll (they get the non-touch clamp with no way to scroll). User decision: fix the two bugs (not add a new setting). Separate branch.
close_reason: Detection fix (maxTouchPoints, f6d5c7e) + controls-duplication fix (split into calvin-ohq) both merged to develop (7bafcdb)

comments.text: Split: (1) DETECTION half DONE — PR #86 (fix/touch-detection-maxtouchpoints, open, awaiting merge): auto now ORs navigator.maxTouchPoints>0. (2) LEGACY-CONTROLS half spun out to calvin-ohq (remove floating RegionControls cluster, consolidate onto header rail) — root-caused this session, needs design-first per user. This bead can close once #86 merges; the controls work lives in calvin-ohq.

title: Dashboard: plugin labels scale with Touch-target size; fix unlock-banner clipping; theme scrollbars
description:
Three dashboard UI fixes reported by user:

1a) Plugin/panel labels (e.g. service title 'Hem för yr') don't scale with the dashboard size setting. Root cause: touchControlSize (small/medium/large, 'Touch target size') only sets --icon-size/--icon-font scoped to RegionControls; DashboardPanel title/subtitle use hardcoded 1.5rem/0.85rem. Fix: expose touchControlSize dashboard-wide (Dashboard.vue) as --panel-title-fs/--panel-subtitle-fs; DashboardPanel reads them. Medium == current (no Default change).

1b) When layout is unlocked, the fixed bottom-center .layout-unlock-banner (Dashboard.vue) occludes the bottom region's content/label. .dashboard-view--unlocked has no CSS today. Fix: reserve bottom padding while unlocked so the banner doesn't cover content.

2) Scrollbars unthemed globally (only TabNavigation has local styling). Fix: add app-wide themed scrollbars to styles/base.css using semantic tokens (--bg-2 track, --line thumb, --ink-3 hover) + Firefox scrollbar-width/color.

Branch: fix/dashboard-label-scale-and-scrollbars

comments.text: Implemented on fix/dashboard-label-scale-and-scrollbars, PR #83 -> develop. 1a: Dashboard.vue tags root dashboard-view--touch-{small|medium|large} exposing --panel-title-fs/--panel-subtitle-fs; DashboardPanel title+subtitle read them (medium==prior 1.5/0.85rem, Default unchanged). 1b: .dashboard-view--unlocked reserves 4.5rem bottom padding so the fixed .layout-unlock-banner stops occluding the bottom label. 2: global themed scrollbars in base.css (semantic tokens + Firefox scrollbar-width/color). Added DashboardLabelScale.spec.js. 952 unit tests, eslint+prettier clean, build green. Visual QA on kiosk still recommended.

Redesigned via brainstorming: unify ALL region chrome under one 5-step scale (xsmall/small/medium/large/xlarge) driven by touchControlSize; proportional rail-height:label:glyph; single control-rail row-height so controls can't misalign; one source of truth via inline :style vars on dashboard root (not class rules); calendar+service labels unified size (medium 1.25rem); remove nonsensical service × close. Clock bar out of scope. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-06-dashboard-region-chrome-scale-design.md

title: Theme reinstall can't upgrade in place: install_theme_from_repo ignores force
description:
The /plugins/github/install route (backend/app/api/routes/plugins/github.py) accepts a `force` param, but the theme path never uses it: install_theme_from_repo() (backend/app/services/theme_installer.py:468) does not accept or forward force, and raises ValueError('Theme {id} is already installed') whenever get_theme_path(id) already exists. install_theme() supports force=True and a check_version downgrade guard, but that plumbing is bypassed on the from-repo path.

Impact: an installed theme can never be upgraded in place. To pick up a new theme version a user must manually uninstall then reinstall. This caused a real support incident: the midnight theme fix (v1.0.0 -> v1.1.0) was merged and served correctly from GitHub, but the running instance kept serving the stale v1.0.0 installed copy at backend/data/themes/midnight/theme.json because reinstall-over-existing errors out. (Compounded by GitHub codeload zip propagation lag right after the merge.)
design: Thread force through install_theme_from_repo(..., force=False) and pass it to install_theme(). Wire the route's existing `force` body param into the theme branch (parity with the plugin branch). Consider: on force reinstall, if new version < installed, still honor check_version unless force explicitly set. Optionally support an explicit 'upgrade' semantic that overwrites when new version >= installed.
acceptance_criteria: POST /plugins/github/install with force=true reinstalls a theme whose dir already exists (overwrites files, updates theme.json on disk). Without force, existing behavior (error) is preserved. Unit test in the theme_installer suite covers force overwrite + downgrade guard.
close_reason: install_theme_from_repo now threads check_version+force and delegates to install_theme (handles overwrite + downgrade guard); route wires force into both theme call sites. 3 tests added. PR #76 merged to develop.

title: Dark-theme text inputs have ~1.16:1 border contrast (WCAG 1.4.11 fail) — near-invisible fields
description: In dark theme, settings text inputs (calendar name, iCal URL, Display name, etc.) render as near-invisible dark rectangles: border rgb(39,49,58) on parent rgb(29,38,45) = ~1.16:1, and input bg rgb(21,28,33) vs parent = ~1.12:1 — both far below WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 for non-text UI components. Fields are only discernible on hover/focus. Reproduced live via Playwright, dark mode, multiple settings pages (shots 29,30).
design: Measured contrast ratios from live rendering (Playwright). Likely a --border-color / input-bg token value in the dark theme block of theme.css.
acceptance_criteria: Raise the input border (and/or background) contrast against the panel in dark theme to >=3:1 so form fields are visibly bounded at rest. Verify calendar/content-source/appearance inputs in dark theme.
close_reason: Added --input-border token (dark #6b7a87 ~3.5:1); pointed all settings form inputs at it.

title: Theme mode switch fires 6 JS errors: GET /api/plugins/None 400 (selectedTheme='None')
description:
Every theme-mode switch (Auto->Dark, Dark->Light, etc.) throws 6 console errors: 'GET /api/plugins/None 400 Bad Request', '[ThemesStore] Failed to fetch theme None: AxiosError', 'Failed to apply custom theme None: AxiosError' (x2 per switch). Reproduced live in-app via Playwright (console captured).

Root cause: frontend/src/composables/useTheme.js:110 does 'if (selectedThemeId.value) applyCustomTheme(selectedThemeId.value)'. When no custom theme is selected the value should be null, but it arrives as the STRING 'None' (Python None serialized to str somewhere in the config round-trip — configStore.selectedTheme default is null per config.js:38/configRegistry.js:105, so a backend/normalization path is stringifying it). 'None' is truthy -> applyCustomTheme('None') -> GET /api/plugins/None (useTheme.js ~60-72 fetch) -> 400 -> caught at :72 and :94. No visible breakage but noisy and indicates broken null-theme state.
design: Verified: live console errors + code trace to useTheme.js:110 truthiness on a 'None' string. Fix at the guard is safe; also chase where null->'None' happens (config save path).
acceptance_criteria: Guard applyTheme against the string 'None'/'null' (treat as no custom theme) AND fix the serialization so selectedTheme stays null. Zero console errors on theme switch. Add a test switching modes with no custom theme selected.
close_reason: normalizeThemeId() maps 'None'/'null'/'' -> null at ingestion + applyCustomTheme guard; value saved back is clean null.

title: Undefined/hardcoded theme CSS: --accent-color, --border, and a hardcoded selected-event ring
description:
Three components reference CSS custom properties that are NEVER defined in any theme (grep across frontend/ for '--accent-color:' and '--border:' returns zero definitions; no fallback given in the var() calls), plus one hardcoded color that doesn't adapt to theme:

(a) frontend/src/components/PluginFieldRenderer.vue:151 (inline style) and :299 (.help-text a) use var(--accent-color). Undefined -> color resolves to inherit, so the intended link/accent affordance renders as plain body text in BOTH themes. Correct token is --accent-primary (theme.css:15 light #2196f3 / :146 dark #42a5f5) — the same file already uses --accent-primary at lines 263/284.

(b) frontend/src/components/settings/shell/SettingsSearch.vue:99,153,166 use border: 1px solid var(--border). Undefined -> shorthand resolves the color to currentColor, so borders render as the text color (black in light, near-white in dark) instead of the intended --border-color (theme.css:10/:141). Sibling components consistently use --border-color.

(c) frontend/src/components/CalendarEventItem.vue:232 hardcodes box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(33,150,243,0.8) (= light-theme accent #2196f3 at 80%). The .focused/:focus states in the same file correctly use var(--accent-primary); .selected does not, so a selected calendar event shows the wrong (light) accent ring in dark theme.
design: All three verified REAL (high conf) by grep-confirmed absence of the token definitions; correct tokens confirmed present. Fixes are one-liners.
acceptance_criteria: --accent-color -> --accent-primary (2x); --border -> --border-color (3x); replace the hardcoded rgba with the accent token (add an --accent-primary-rgb token if the 80% alpha must be preserved). Verify selected-event ring and settings-search borders in both themes.
close_reason: --accent-color -> --accent-primary (2x); --border -> --border-color (3x); selected-event ring uses color-mix accent token.

title: imap plugin: test_connection blocks the event loop (no thread offload/timeout)
description:
In ../calvin-plugins/imap/plugin.py ~lines 519-523, the async classmethod test_connection makes fully synchronous imaplib calls (IMAP4_SSL(), login(), select(), close(), logout()) directly on the event loop — no asyncio.to_thread, no timeout. The same class does it correctly in run_scheduled_task (~line 267: await asyncio.to_thread(self._check_emails_sync), with a comment noting imaplib is synchronous).

Reachable: management.py:1152 does a bare 'await plugin_class.test_connection(config)' with no wait_for/thread, wired to the 'Test connection' button (POST /api/plugins/imap/test). Python's default socket timeout is None; against a firewalled host the OS TCP connect timeout (~75-130s on Linux) blocks the uvicorn loop the whole time, queuing every other dashboard request (calendar refresh, photo cycling, all API).
design: Verified REAL, high conf. Existing test_imap.py TestConnectionTest monkeypatches IMAP4_SSL with MagicMock, so the blocking pattern is invisible to CI.
acceptance_criteria: Wrap the blocking imaplib calls in asyncio.to_thread and apply a connect/login timeout. Add a test that exercises the real (non-mocked) sync-call path or asserts to_thread is used. Consider a host-side asyncio.wait_for around test_connection generally.
close_reason: test_connection now offloads blocking imaplib via asyncio.to_thread with a 10s socket timeout on IMAP4_SSL; logout is best-effort. Fixed in calvin-plugins branch audit/overnight-2026-07-05. Tests assert timeout kwarg + to_thread.

title: Plugin uninstall never removes pip packages; failed install can leak them too
description:
backend/app/services/plugin_installer.py manages pip deps declared in plugin.json dependencies.packages, but the packages are never uninstalled.

(a) uninstall_plugin() (~lines 342-357) is only: check path exists -> shutil.rmtree(plugin_path). It never reads the manifest's _installed_packages (persisted at install ~line 251) and never pip-uninstalls. Every uninstall leaves its packages resident in the shared venv. docs/plugins/PLUGIN_PERSISTENCE_AND_RESTART.md lists the uninstall lifecycle (stop instances, delete DB rows, unload module, remove dir, emit event) with pip removal simply absent — no comment says retention is intentional.

(b) Incomplete rollback: in install_plugin(), _install_pip_requirements() runs first (~249), then the manifest write open()/json.dump (~254-256) can raise (disk full / perms on the RPi SD card). The except handler (~260-265) does shutil.rmtree(plugin_path) and re-raises but never pip-uninstalls the packages already installed — and _installed_packages never reached disk, so no later pass can clean them either. The management API's post-install steps (import, DB registration) failing and calling back into uninstall_plugin() is the more realistic trigger, and that path also leaks packages (see a).
design: Both verified REAL, high confidence, by adversarial refuter. _installed_packages is written to plugin.json but grep confirms it is only ever written, never read for cleanup. Impact on RPi: SD-card disk bloat across install/uninstall cycles; version conflicts when a later plugin needs a different pinned version and pip silently up/downgrades a leaked package, breaking the original plugin's deps.
acceptance_criteria: uninstall_plugin() reads _installed_packages and pip-uninstalls them (guarding against packages still required by another installed plugin); install rollback uninstalls any packages it installed before removing the dir. Document the shared-venv policy either way. Tests for both paths.
close_reason: uninstall_plugin now pip-uninstalls _installed_packages (skipping ones other plugins need); install rollback uninstalls any packages it installed before rmtree. Best-effort helpers added; shared-venv policy documented. 4 tests added.

title: [bug] Mode HUD flashes wrong mode on reload (e.g. 'Calendar Mode' HUD appears after F5 in Settings)
description:
REPRO: while in Settings, press F5 (reload). A transient input-echo HUD (e.g. 'Calendar Mode') pops centre/bottom screen even though you're in settings with chrome visible.

SUSPECTED ROOT CAUSE (systematic-debugging Phase 1, not yet confirmed/fixed): frontend/src/components/NotificationSystem.vue is the input-echo/mode HUD. On reload the Pinia stores rehydrate; modeStore.currentMode defaults to CALENDAR (stores/mode.js:14) before the persisted mode restores, and configStore.shouldShowUI is briefly false during hydration. The watcher on [currentMode, isFullscreen, fullscreenMode] (~L211) and the shouldShowUI watcher (~L232) call showModeChange(), whose only guard is 'if (configStore.shouldShowUI) return' (L207). During the hydration window that guard passes, so show('mode', 'Calendar Mode') fires and the HUD flashes. Settings isn't even handled in getModeMessage() (defaults to 'Dashboard'), reinforcing that the HUD shouldn't surface here at all.

LIKELY FIX DIRECTIONS (pick after confirming): (a) gate the mode-HUD watchers behind an 'app hydrated/initialized' flag so they don't fire during the initial settle; (b) suppress the HUD when currentMode === SETTINGS; (c) debounce/skip the first watcher tick after mount. Confirm the race first (instrument the watcher + shouldShowUI/currentMode at mount) before choosing.

CONTEXT: introduced/adjacent to commit 41938d3 'feat(notifications): split toast into annunciator rail + input-echo HUD'. Files: NotificationSystem.vue (watchers L199-245, show() L167), stores/mode.js, stores/config.js (shouldShowUI).
notes:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (code-read, not just suspected): (1) Settings.vue never calls setMode(SETTINGS), so on reload currentMode stays at its default CALENDAR — that's why the flashed label is 'Calendar Mode'. (2) showUI defaults to true; fetchConfig() applies the persisted value, and applyConfigPayload(useDefaults:true) assigns every field unconditionally. On kiosk/chrome-hidden setups (persisted showUI=false) this flips showUI true->false async (post-network), firing the shouldShowUI watcher -> showModeChange(), whose only guard (shouldShowUI already false) passes -> HUD flashes. Not settings-specific; any reload with persisted showUI=false reproduces it. Note the misfire is async (network-timed), so a mount-time gate cannot catch it — the gate must release on config-load completion.

FIX (direction (a) from the bead): added config-store 'hydrated' latch, set true one nextTick after the first fetchConfig() settles (deferred so the same-flush showUI watcher still sees hydrated=false). showModeChange() now bails while !hydrated. Covers both watchers and both routes; rejected (b) suppress-SETTINGS (currentMode is CALENDAR, not SETTINGS, and dashboard reloads also flash) and (c) debounce-first-tick (fire is async, not first-tick).

Files: frontend/src/stores/config.js, frontend/src/components/NotificationSystem.vue. Tests: added 2 boot-hydration cases in NotificationSystem.spec.js (1 was a failing repro first). Full frontend unit suite green (943), eslint + prettier clean. Branch: fix/mode-hud-flash-on-reload.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #77 (merged to develop, bc817ac). Added config-store 'hydrated' latch; showModeChange() bails until the initial config load settles. Full frontend suite green, CI green.

title: Built-in themes: tint the modern shell + resolve Dark-theme vs dark-mode overlap
description: The built-in themes (Ocean/Forest/Sunset) only recolor the accent on the redesigned shell; a deeper IA smell exists between the 'Dark' theme and dark mode. Two related sub-problems, discovered while fixing the calvin-plugins midnight-theme (added focus + redesign surface tokens; PR pending).
design:
## Background

Theme SELECTION (Light/Dark/Ocean/Forest/Sunset) and light/dark MODE are two
independent systems:

- MODE (`themeMode` in useTheme.js) toggles the `.dark` class on <html>, which
  is what actually drives the redesign surface tokens (`--bg-1`, `--ink`,
  `--line`, …) defined in `frontend/src/styles/theme.css`.
- SELECTION (`selectedThemeId`) layers a theme's `variables` on top via
  `applyCustomTheme()` — writing each key verbatim as `--<key>` on :root.

The built-in themes (`backend/data/themes/builtin.json`) only set the LEGACY
token set (`bg-primary`, `text-primary`, `accent-primary`, calendar-*, …) plus
`focus`. The redesigned UI reads the NEW semantic tokens (`--bg-1`, `--ink`,
`--line`, `--focus`, `--ok/warn/err`) in ~66 files vs ~11 for the legacy set.

## Problem 1 — expressive themes don't tint the modern surfaces (data fix)

Ocean/Forest/Sunset each carry a surface tint in their palette (e.g. Ocean
`bg-primary: #e8f4f8`), but the modern shell reads `--bg-1` which they don't
set. Net effect on the redesigned shell:

- Ocean + light mode  → WHITE surfaces, blue accent (tint ignored)
- Ocean + dark mode   → NEUTRAL dark surfaces (from `.dark`), blue accent

FIX: add the redesign surface tokens to each of Ocean/Forest/Sunset, in BOTH
`variables` and `dark_mode`, mapped from the theme's existing palette:
  bg-1 <- bg-primary, bg-2 <- bg-secondary, bg-0 <- a shade darker,
  ink <- text-primary, ink-2 <- text-secondary, ink-3 <- text-tertiary,
  line <- border-color, line-soft <- a softer divider,
  ok <- accent-secondary, warn <- accent-warning, err <- accent-error.
  (focus already present.)
Leave `light` alone (base; no-op on modern shell is correct).
This is exactly the fix applied to the midnight-theme (theme.json v1.1.0).
Covered by `backend/tests/integration/test_api_themes.py`.

## Problem 2 — "Dark" theme vs dark MODE overlap (design pass)

Selecting the "Dark" THEME (`selectedThemeId='dark'`) does NOT add the `.dark`
class (that's `themeMode`), so on the modern shell you'd get white surfaces +
dark legacy bits + amber accent — a mixed/broken state. Two overlapping dark
mechanisms confuse the model.

Options to brainstorm (needs a design decision, touches Display settings +
useTheme.js — do NOT bundle with Problem 1):
- selecting the "Dark"/"Light" theme sets the corresponding mode, OR
- drop Light/Dark as selectable themes entirely (the mode toggle covers them),
  leaving only expressive themes as selectable.

## Reference
- useTheme.js `applyCustomTheme()` (lines 59-96): `--<key>` loop + focus special-casing.
- theme.css: legacy tokens (~4-28 / .dark 133-159) vs redesign tokens (30-49 / .dark 161-176).
- builtin.json: the 5 built-ins.

title: Build shared ui/IconButton primitive; migrate ad-hoc icon buttons
description:
Create a single ui/IconButton.vue primitive and migrate the scattered square-icon-button implementations onto it. These duplicated implementations are the ROOT CAUSE of the calendar/service header-button mismatch (calvin-nxs) and the broader service-region drift (calvin-0wr).

CURRENT DUPLICATES (different sizes/tokens/radii):
- .dashboard-panel__icon-button (frontend/src/styles/main.css) — service/panel header buttons (just aligned in calvin-nxs, but should become IconButton)
- .calendar-header__nav (CalendarView.vue) — 1.75rem square nav/expand
- RegionViewOptions.vue trigger — 1.75rem 'tune' trigger
- RegionControls.vue .cbtn — touch nav cluster (sized by touchControlSize)
- ThemePicker.vue trigger/chevron and other one-off icon buttons

PRIMITIVE (ui/IconButton.vue): square button using the sizing vocabulary — default ~1.75rem square, --radius-sm/8px, font ~1.05rem, semantic tokens (--bg-2/--line/--ink), hover --focus-edge, :focus-visible ring var(--focus). Props: variant ('default'|'primary' -> --focus bg + --focus-ink), size (optional; e.g. map to touchControlSize for the dashboard cluster), :aria-label (required), disabled. Slot for the glyph/SVG.

MIGRATE call sites above to compose IconButton, deleting the bespoke CSS. .cbtn/touch cluster: fold RegionControls buttons into <IconButton :size> so touchControlSize still drives dashboard size.

ENABLES/relates: calvin-0wr (service regions adopt IconButton instead of re-styling); supersedes the one-off fix in calvin-nxs (closed).

DONE = one primitive; no bespoke square-icon-button CSS remains in the migrated components; all icon buttons visually consistent at default; existing behavior (touchControlSize sizing, focus states) preserved; tests/lint/build green.
notes: Primitive DELIVERED: frontend/src/components/ui/IconButton.vue + 7 unit tests (commit 9e7285b, pushed). Built via subagent-driven TDD; task review clean (spec compliant, quality approved). API: label(req)/variant(default|primary|ghost|danger)/size(sm|md|lg)/shape(square|circle)/active/disabled; single <button> root so aria-*/@click fall through; token-styled. Spec docs/design/2026-07-04-iconbutton-primitive.md, plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-04-iconbutton-primitive.md. REMAINING = migrate the ~8 call-site families onto it (deferred by design): service regions via calvin-0wr; others (panel-header, closers, drag handles, touch cluster w/ size escape-hatch) as follow-up tranches.
close_reason: All tranches merged. Final closers tranche via PR #82 (merge 1628c01): 7 bespoke close/× buttons -> ui/IconButton, bespoke CSS deleted (net -141 lines). No bespoke square-icon-button CSS remains; primitive delivered + all call-site families migrated. CI green, 949 unit tests pass.

description:

title: Model rolling as a windowing modifier (base view × rolling), add rolling-week
description:
Rolling is currently a 4th value of the single `calendarViewMode` field (month/week/day/rolling), which makes it mutually exclusive with the base views and asymmetric in the on-calendar toggle (you can cycle *out* of rolling to month, but not *into* it). Rolling isn't a peer view — it's a windowing choice orthogonal to granularity.

## Model
Two independent axes:
- Base granularity (the on-calendar toggle): Month / Week / Day
- Windowing (a Settings behavior): Fixed calendar period vs. Rolling window anchored to now

'Rolling' = roll the next unit down:
- Month + rolling → rolls WEEKS (N weeks from the current week) = today's existing rolling behavior
- Week + rolling → rolls DAYS (next N days from today) = NEW 'rolling week' render path
- Day + rolling → n/a

## Work
- Split `calendarViewMode` into base view (month/week/day) + a `rollingWindow` on/off flag (reuse the existing `calendarWeeks` count; add a days count for rolling-week). Keep back-compat: legacy 'rolling' value maps to base=month + rollingWindow=on.
- Keep the on-calendar toggle strictly Month/Week/Day; expose rolling on/off + count in Settings → Content → Calendar display (ContentSettings.vue).
- Implement rolling-week: N days starting today. NOTE design decision: rolling days break fixed Mon–Sun weekday columns (today lands in column 1), so headers become per-day dates — effectively a 'next N days' agenda strip rather than a weekday grid. Decide deliberately.
- Update CalendarView.vue calendarDays/loadEvents/navigation/currentMonthYear/isCurrentPeriod to key off (base, rolling) instead of the 4-value field.

## Context
Follow-up from the calendar header/fullscreen/rolling-fix work (calvin-00s). The overlap-cache bug that made rolling drop events on navigation was already fixed separately in plugin_calendar_service (full-coverage instead of >=50% overlap).

title: Focused service (web-service) regions show no focus-light glow
description: User-pinpointed root cause of the 'multiregion focus light broken / rightmost region doesn't bleed' report: a region rendering a web SERVICE never received the focus glow (only a thin border), so it looked like the glow was missing/not bleeding. title: Focus-light glow clipped on split sub-regions (later siblings paint over it)

description:

title: Kiosk region-focus targets global active screen (read/write asymmetry)
description: Found in dd9.4 whole-branch review. Data-loss-safe (no screens dropped). Region-view being global was an explicit dd9.4 non-goal, so this is expected-ish, but the mismatch is a latent UX quirk.

title: Tree-wide: replace deprecated datetime.utcnow() with datetime.now(UTC)
description: datetime.utcnow() is deprecated in Python 3.12+ and emits DeprecationWarning. The codebase uses it pervasively (db_models.py model defaults incl. KioskDB.last_seen, and app/services/kiosk_registry.py record_kiosk). Must be migrated TREE-WIDE in one pass, not per-file: mixing naive datetime.utcnow() with tz-aware datetime.now(timezone.utc) in the same column causes naive-vs-aware comparison TypeErrors. Surfaced during dd9.2 reviews (Task 1 + Task 2).
acceptance_criteria: All datetime.utcnow() replaced with datetime.now(timezone.utc) (or a shared helper) across models + services in one consistent pass; datetime columns are uniformly tz-aware; no naive/aware mixing; tests green.

title: SSE push channel for kiosks (upgrade the version-poll nudge)
description: Optional upgrade to the display-agent config-apply mechanism. The core per-kiosk model (dd9) uses a version-poll nudge (Option 1): server exposes a per-kiosk deviceConfigVersion (ETag/If-None-Match on /api/config?kiosk=<id>), the agent fast-polls it (~10-15s) and applies xrandr/backlight on change. This issue tracks replacing/augmenting that poll with a real SSE push channel so applies are instant instead of within one poll cycle.
design: Add a general GET /api/kiosk/<id>/events SSE stream (StreamingResponse text/event-stream already proven in system.py). Bridge the existing in-memory asyncio event bus (docs/EVENT_SYSTEM.md) -> SSE so a per-kiosk config change emits a 'reload' event the agent consumes immediately. Agent needs reconnect/backoff + heartbeat handling. Potential additional wins: push config changes to the browser frontend too (replace its 30s configPollInterval), live status/health of kiosks, plugin data refresh push. Evaluate whether one SSE channel can serve agent + browser.
acceptance_criteria: A kiosk's device-physical config change is applied by the display-agent within ~1s via SSE push (no reliance on the version-poll cadence), with graceful reconnect. Version-poll remains as fallback when SSE is unavailable.
