Minor follow-up noted (fold into Part B or defer): at xlarge in a very narrow region the weather-forecast day-columns crowd because grid-auto-columns min-width stays rem while content grows.

REMAINING = Part B: card-grid size control + mealie clipping fix (bigger cards + scroll, keyboard-nav nuance). Separate PR, needs its own design/brainstorm. NOTE: current CardGrid.vue has NO fixed row height in its own CSS — the ~82px clip comes from a height constraint imposed by the region/panel host, not the card.

comments.author: Simon Österberg
comments.text: Part B shipped → PR #85 (branch feat/card-grid-size-control, base develop). card-grid fit-clamp (whole-row clamp non-touch / scroll+snap+shade touch) + per-region 5-step card-size control. Live-verified end-to-end incl. two bugs caught live (row-collapse defeating the clamp; clampServiceView stripping cardSize). Final review (opus) ready-to-merge; non-blocking region-enlarge fix landed. 978 FE tests green. Fast-follows filed: weather/item-list fit-clamp; touch-detection+unlock-controls bug.

title: Search dropdown has no background, blends over settings spine
description: The search dropdown renders without a solid background, so its contents bleed visually over the settings spine behind it. Needs an opaque surface background (and likely proper z-index/elevation) so results are legible against the settings layout.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Simon Österberg
comments.text: Fixed — PR #80 squash-merged to develop (commit fbcc3c0). SettingsSearch was styled against nonexistent --surface* tokens so the results dropdown resolved 'background: var(--surface)' to transparent and bled over the spine; mapped to semantic tokens (dropdown+bar --bg-2, hint --bg-1) with a focus-tinted result hover. Visually verified via Playwright: opaque dropdown occluding content behind it.

title: Display settings tile gets clipped when selected
description: The Display settings tile is visually clipped when it enters the selected state — part of the tile (likely an outline/scale/box-shadow on selection) overflows or is cut off by the container's clip/overflow boundary.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Simon Österberg
comments.text: Fixed — PR #80 squash-merged to develop (commit fbcc3c0). Root cause: .category-rail was an overflow-y:auto scroll container, which clips both axes and cut the selected tile's outward FocusPanel glow into a box. The rail only needs to scroll on a wide-short kiosk (calvin-g7v); the 6 categories fit on a normal viewport. Fix: default overflow:visible (full unclipped glow, matches dashboard focused-region language), overflow-y:auto only under @media (max-height:600px) and (min-width:769px). Verified via Playwright at 1280x720 (full glow, no box) and 800x480 (rail scrolls, g7v preserved). User confirmed 'much better'.

title: Revisit fullscreen modes after screen/region rework
description: Migrated from GitHub #35. Precondition (land #34 per-screen region layouts) is now met — DashboardRegion.vue et al. shipped. Legacy fullscreen modes still coexist: modeStore.fullscreenMode gated in Dashboard.vue (MODES.PHOTOS -> PhotoSlideshow is-fullscreen; MODES.WEB_SERVICES -> WebServiceViewer cycling all services), triggered by keybinds mode_photos/mode_web_services + in-app toggle, hiding chrome. Now actionable as a design decision.
design: Directions (undecided): (1) Leave as-is — screens = curated layouts, fullscreen = transient blow-up. (2) Unify under screens via per-screen kiosk:true; treat mode_* keybinds as 'switch to first kiosk screen' (loses service cycling unless per-region rotation built). (3) Hybrid — fullscreen stays a runtime overlay but rebuilt on a single ad-hoc kiosk screen (one rendering pipeline; cycling becomes a screen property). Open Qs: is fullscreen service-cycling still wanted? should kiosk/chrome-hidden be a screen prop, view-state, or both? must keybinds keep 'mode' semantics or become 'switch to screen X'?

title: Clock Bar: drag-and-drop ordering for plugin tiles
description: Migrated from GitHub #47 (follow-up to PR #46, which added the Clock Bar settings + per-instance visibility toggle). The Bar Items UI toggles tiles on/off but order is implicit (driven by display_order set elsewhere). Users should reorder tiles directly with drag handles, persisting across reloads. NOTE: wording predates a ClockBarSettings.vue rework — re-confirm current component shape before implementing.
design: Two options: (1) Reuse display_order via pluginsApi.updatePluginInstanceOrder — no new state, but couples clock-bar order to e.g. Services panel ordering. (2) New global clockBarOrder: [serviceId,...] config key — independent ordering, but extra key to reconcile on add/remove. Author leaned toward (2) for clean separation; worth a short design discussion first.
acceptance_criteria: Drag handle on each row in Clock Bar bar-items UI; order persists across reload; live ClockBarHorizontal/ClockBarVertical reflect new order without hard refresh; hidden tiles can still be reordered.

title: iCal URL field duplicates its placeholder as static help text; orphaned '/' search hint on touch kiosk
description:
Two minor settings polish issues (reproduced live via Playwright):
(a) Content Sources -> Calendars: the URL input shows 'Generic iCal feed (Proton, Outlook, etc.)' as BOTH its placeholder and identical static help text directly below — the same string twice when the field is empty, adding nothing.
(b) Every settings category shows a lone <kbd>/</kbd> hint at the far right of the search row, visually detached from the search input so it reads as an orphaned separator/broken element. On a touch-first kiosk with no physical keyboard the '/' focus shortcut is irrelevant, yet the hint is always visible.
design: Both confirmed via live Playwright screenshots (shots 03,04,28). Low-risk polish; grouped as one settings-polish bead.
acceptance_criteria: (a) Either drop the duplicate help text or make it distinct from the placeholder. (b) Hide the '/' hint on touch/kiosk (or when no keyboard), or visually attach it inside the search field.
close_reason: Placeholder no longer reuses plugin description (falls to URL example); '/' hint hidden on touch via useTouchCapability.

title: 800x480 kiosk viewport: modal Save/Cancel below the fold + settings body overflows (no constrained scroll)
description:
On an 800x480 RPi touchscreen, two related layout problems (reproduced live via Playwright at 800x480):
(a) The Add-source InstanceModal's Save/Cancel (.modal-actions) sit below the visible area. NOTE (verified in code): .instance-modal has max-height:90vh; overflow-y:auto and .modal-actions (InstanceModal.vue:133) is INSIDE it, so the buttons ARE reachable by scrolling WITHIN the modal — this is NOT a hard 'cannot submit' blocker as first reported. But there is no sticky footer, so on a short touchscreen the primary action is off-screen with no visual cue to scroll.
(b) The settings page body (settings-body) expands to content height (~988px) with overflow:visible and no viewport-constrained scroll region, so Device/Maintenance sidebar items and the plugin list sit below the fold, requiring page-scroll that may not exist in a chromeless kiosk.
design: (a) DOWNGRADED from the UX pass's P1: code shows the modal scrolls internally so Save is reachable — real issue is affordance, not a submit blocker. (b) confirmed via full-page render height 988px vs 480px viewport.
acceptance_criteria: (a) Make .modal-actions a sticky footer within the modal (or ensure it's always visible at 90vh). (b) Constrain the settings layout to the viewport with an internal scroll region. Verify both at 800x480.
close_reason: (a) modal-actions is now a sticky footer. (b) scoped the max-height:600px page-scroll override to also require max-width:768px so a wide-short kiosk keeps the constrained internal scroll; CategoryRail scrolls independently. Verified via build/lint; live 800x480 visual verification recommended as final acceptance.

title: Close (x) buttons lack aria-labels (fullscreen calendar dismiss, Add-source modal)
description: The fullscreen-calendar dismiss button and the InstanceModal close button (InstanceModal.vue:12 <button class=btn-close-modal>x</button>) use a bare 'x' glyph with no aria-label (DOM query confirmed aria:null). Screen readers announce 'times'/nothing with no context. Relevant for kiosks run with AT enabled. Reproduced live via Playwright DOM inspection.
design: Confirmed via live DOM query (aria:null) on the fullscreen x and the modal btn-close-modal:12.
acceptance_criteria: Add aria-label='Close' (or 'Exit fullscreen') to these buttons; audit other icon-only buttons for the same. A quick eslint-plugin-vuejs-accessibility rule could enforce it.
close_reason: aria-label added to InstanceModal close, CalendarView + WebServiceViewer fullscreen dismiss. PhotoSlideshow already had one.

title: Feature: Home Assistant sensors plugin (metric-dashboard + statusbar)
description:
PROBLEM: Households running Home Assistant have temp/door/energy/presence entities that belong on the wall but are inaccessible from Calvin, forcing a separate HA dashboard device.
FIT: Self-hosted HA is common in the RPi wall-display demographic; three sensor tiles alongside weather/meals completes a home-status overview.
SHAPE: New calvin-plugins/home-assistant ServicePlugin. instance_config_schema: ha_url, access_token(password), entity_ids, columns, per-entity warn_above/error_above. fetch() calls HA local REST (GET /api/states/{entity}, Bearer token) and maps {friendly_name,state,unit_of_measurement}->{label,value,unit,status} for metric-dashboard. scan_options classmethod calls GET /api/states to enumerate entities for a select-scan UI. statusbar_schema exposes a subset to the clock bar. test_connection validates the token before save.
REUSE: metric-dashboard renderer, statusbar status kind, scan_options/select-scan (chromecast), test_connection classmethod, the 'http call in fetch' pattern (weather, mealie).
EFFORT: M. Risk: heterogeneous entity types need a coercion step in fetch(); default to no status coloring unless thresholds set.

title: Feature: countdown / days-until plugin (metric-dashboard + statusbar)
description:
PROBLEM: Important household dates (birthday in 3 days, trip in 12) are invisible on the wall; no glanceable 'time until' surface exists.
FIT: Emotionally resonant, zero ongoing maintenance once set. The ok->warn->error status-color system maps naturally to far->soon->imminent, giving at-a-glance urgency without clutter.
SHAPE: New calvin-plugins/countdown ServicePlugin, no external deps. instance_config_schema: events (multiline 'Name|YYYY-MM-DD|emoji' parsed in configure()), warn_days(14), error_days(3). fetch() computes days-remaining -> {metrics:[{icon,label,value,unit:'days',status}], statusbar:[{...nearest...}]}. metrics feed the existing metric-dashboard renderer; statusbar feeds the clock-bar status renderer. get_schedule_config() daily-midnight job updates without a page reload.
REUSE: metric-dashboard renderer (icon/label/value/unit/status lamp), statusbar status kind, system-monitor's _status() threshold pattern.
EFFORT: S. Risk: multiline config UX — confirm PluginFieldRenderer supports a textarea field type, else add it.

title: Feature: departure-board display kind + public-transit plugin
description:
PROBLEM: 'When's the next bus?' is a top morning glance. item-list renders static strings — no live countdown from an ISO departure time, no realtime-vs-scheduled or route/destination layout.
FIT: Compact transit board in the clock bar or a panel tile is high-delight for commuters; GTFS-RT data is free/public across many regions.
SHAPE: (1) New DepartureBoard.vue renderer: {departures:[{route,headsign,departure_time(ISO),platform,realtime}]}; client-side setInterval recomputes 'X min' countdowns; route badge + destination + countdown + realtime dot. Register in rendererRegistry.js + SUPPORTED_DISPLAY_KINDS. (2) New calvin-plugins/transit ServicePlugin (configurable api_url, stop_id) returning next N departures; statusbar_schema status shows nearest departure ('bus 7m') in the clock bar; scan_options classmethod (mirrors chromecast select-scan) to discover nearby stops.
REUSE: statusbar_schema + status kind (PluginStatusbarItems), scan_options contract (chromecast), get_schedule_config().
EFFORT: M. Risk: stop-ID discovery varies by agency — provide manual-entry fallback.

title: Feature: RSS/Atom feed plugin (item-list kind)
description:
PROBLEM: No way to show time-ordered text content (news, blog updates, a private family-announcements feed, home-automation alerts). The item-list display kind exists but has zero plugin consumers.
FIT: Near-universal home-dashboard use case; works fully self-hosted with no cloud account.
SHAPE: New calvin-plugins/rss-feed ServicePlugin; feedparser in plugin.json dependencies.packages. fetch() returns {items:[{title,date,url,summary}]}. display_schema {kind:'item-list', data_path:'$.items', item:{label_path:'$.title', timestamp_path:'$.date', url_path:'$.url'}, link_action:'embed'} — existing EmbedOverlay/HandoffOverlay in ItemList.vue handle tap-to-read (kiosk-safe). instance_config_schema: feed_url,title,max_items(10),refresh_minutes; instance_identity:['feed_url'] for multiple feeds. get_schedule_config() drives refresh.
REUSE: ItemList.vue + useLinkOpen (embed/handoff overlays), applyFormat time-12h, get_schedule_config/run_scheduled_task (imap, system-monitor).
EFFORT: S. Risk: graceful handling of malformed/redirected feeds in fetch().

title: Feature: event-agenda display kind + calendar-agenda service plugin
description:
PROBLEM: Calendar data is locked in calendar mode; there's no glanceable 'next N events' tile in a services panel. Existing card-grid/item-list kinds have no day grouping, source colors, or all-day vs timed distinction.
FIT: After weather, 'what's on today?' is the top home wall-display use case — a compact agenda tile alongside weather/meals is core to a kitchen dashboard.
SHAPE: (1) New EventAgenda.vue renderer in frontend/src/components/plugins/renderers/ with contract {kind:'event-agenda', data_path:'$.events', item:{date_path,time_path,title_path,color_path,all_day_path}}; groups by date (Today/Tomorrow/weekday) with colored chips; reuse applyFormat + time-12h/24h formatters. Register in rendererRegistry.js AND SUPPORTED_DISPLAY_KINDS in backend/app/plugins/definitions.py (kind-sync test enforces both). (2) New calvin-plugins/calendar-agenda ServicePlugin importing app.services.plugin_calendar_service for a configurable lookahead, shaping into the agenda payload; scheduler via get_schedule_config()/run_scheduled_task().
REUSE: plugin_calendar_service (already used by routes/calendar.py), formatters.js, CalendarEventItem patterns.
EFFORT: M. Risk: keep the service plugin's import of app.services clean/decoupled from internal models; update test_display_kind_sync.py.

title: Photo frame shows 'No images available' on kiosk reboot instead of last-known image (no cache fallback)
description: frontend/src/stores/images.js has NO localStorage cache fallback (unlike webServices.js/calendar.js which use utils/cache.js with TTL). fetchImages/fetchCurrentImage catch, set error.value, and rethrow with no cached fallback and no persistence. On an RPi kiosk the frontend systemd unit can come up before the backend, and a page refresh during backend maintenance hits the same path: with images.value=[] and currentImage=null, PhotoSlideshow.vue renders the 'No images available' placeholder on the wall display. Local images (/api/images/{id}) need a live backend so there's no browser-cache mitigation either.
design: Verified REAL, high conf. In-memory Pinia state survives a transient outage while the app stays alive; the broken case is fresh load/refresh when the backend is down.
acceptance_criteria: Add a localStorage cache in fetchImages/fetchCurrentImage mirroring webServices.js (store last image list + current, serve stale on failure/offline). Wall display should show the last-known photo through a transient backend outage.
close_reason: fetchImages/fetchCurrentImage cache the wall-display (__all__) feed + current image (24h TTL) and serve stale on failure. Mirrors webServices/calendar cache pattern. Tests added.

title: Frontend type-check is a no-op: 'type-check' script runs eslint, not vue-tsc
description: frontend/package.json defines "type-check": "npm run lint" (which runs eslint .), so 'make type-check' / CI never actually type-checks TypeScript/Vue types — vue-tsc is never invoked. Any .ts/.vue type error goes undetected. Backend mypy is clean; frontend has zero type-checking despite the target implying otherwise.
design: Confirmed by the test/lint runner: mypy clean (72 files), but vue-tsc never runs; type-check target aliases lint. Not test-infra noise — a real coverage gap.
acceptance_criteria: Point type-check at vue-tsc --noEmit (or tsc) and fix whatever it surfaces; keep lint separate. Wire it into CI/Makefile so it actually gates.
notes: TRIAGE (overnight-audit session): deferred as non-trivial. vue-tsc is not a dependency and there is no tsconfig/jsconfig; the codebase is JS (only src/api/types.ts is generated TS). Enabling real type-checking means adding vue-tsc + a tsconfig with checkJs and then fixing whatever it surfaces — potentially large and uncertain, not an 'easy fix'. Recommend a dedicated PR: (1) add vue-tsc dep + tsconfig scoped narrowly (e.g. checkJs off initially, type-check src/api + .ts only), (2) wire into CI/Makefile, (3) expand coverage incrementally.

title: themes.js store: fetchInstalledThemes reads wrong field and github install sends wrong key (dead but broken)
description:
frontend/src/stores/themes.js has two real correctness bugs, currently DEAD CODE (zero call sites outside the store), but latent traps if ever wired up:
(a) ~line 52-53: line 52 filters response.data.plugins to type=='theme' but discards the result (writes back onto the response object), then line 53 assigns installedThemes.value = response.data.themes || [] — but GET /api/plugins/installed returns {plugins:[...], total} with NO 'themes' key (confirmed via live curl + PluginListResponse model). So installedThemes is always [].
(b) ~line 115-119: installThemeFromGithub POSTs {theme_path: ...} to /api/plugins/github/install, but the handler (github.py:175,182) requires plugin_path and 400s otherwise. The working UI path (pluginsApi.installPluginFromGitHub) correctly sends plugin_path.
design: Both REAL bugs, high conf, but DEAD CODE (no user impact today). Filed as latent cleanup so a future 'themes UI' effort doesn't inherit silent breakage.
acceptance_criteria: Either delete the dead functions or fix them: read response.data.plugins (already filtered) for (a); send plugin_path for (b). If theme management is planned, wire these to the UI with tests.
close_reason: fetchInstalledThemes reads response.data.plugins; github install sends plugin_path. Tests updated.

title: IframeRenderer embeds plugin URLs with no sandbox or referrerpolicy
description: frontend/src/components/plugins/renderers/IframeRenderer.vue (~lines 3-13) renders <iframe :src=url> with NO sandbox and NO referrerpolicy attribute. url comes from schema.url (install-time, user-chosen) OR schema.url_path — the latter is resolved from the plugin's runtime fetch() data, so a plugin can change the embedded origin on any refresh WITHOUT user action. On a kiosk, a compromised/malicious plugin can point the frame at an attacker origin that scripts window.parent, reads the session, or breaks the kiosk. Missing referrerpolicy also leaks the kiosk origin to every embedded page. Distinct from calvin-ks7 (that covers the load-failure 'open in new window' handoff anchor, not the embed's sandbox).
design: PARTIALLY REAL / defense-in-depth (high conf). No v-html anywhere in renderers (grep clean); img :src in ImageWithCaption can't execute script. The url_path runtime-controlled origin is what lifts this above 'user chose the URL'.
acceptance_criteria: Add referrerpolicy='no-referrer' unconditionally and a best-effort sandbox baseline (e.g. sandbox='allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms allow-popups'); document the url_path runtime-origin risk. Test that the attributes are present.
close_reason: iframe gets referrerpolicy=no-referrer + sandbox='allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms allow-popups'.

title: Weather plugins blank the whole widget on one malformed/unexpected API field
description:
Two weather plugins in ../calvin-plugins do unguarded parsing in _shape_for_display, so a single bad field aborts the entire payload (the outer fetch() try/except returns {error:...} and the widget shows an error state instead of degrading):

(a) yr_weather/plugin.py ~line 453: datetime.fromisoformat(time_str.replace('Z','+00:00')).date() runs inside the timeseries loop with no try/except. One malformed timestamp raises ValueError mid-loop; the already-computed 'current' block is discarded and the whole forecast blanks. (mealie/plugin.py:254-257 wraps the same parse in try/except — the intended pattern.)

(b) weather/plugin.py ~lines 332-344 and 352-354: indexes current_data['weather'][0] and current_data['main'][...] with no bounds/key guards. An unexpected 200-response shape (OWM schema change, free-tier partial response, empty weather array) raises KeyError/IndexError and blanks the widget.
design: (a) PARTIALLY REAL, (b) REAL, both high conf. Neither plugin has a test covering the malformed-input path (fixtures always well-formed).
acceptance_criteria: Per-entry try/except (skip the bad row, keep good ones) for yr_weather; input guards / .get() chains for weather. Add tests feeding a malformed timestamp and an empty/missing weather+main to assert graceful degradation.
close_reason: yr_weather wraps per-entry fromisoformat (skip bad row); weather (OWM) guards weather[0]/main with .get() + wraps each forecast entry. calvin-plugins branch audit/overnight-2026-07-05. Tests added for both.

title: Plugin contract: instance_identity keys not validated; instance-id suffix not re-checked for uniqueness
description:
Two latent correctness gaps in plugin instance identity handling:

(a) backend/app/plugins/definitions.py:143 declares instance_identity: list[str] | None with NO field_validator cross-checking its entries against instance_config_schema keys (unlike display_schema/statusbar_schema, which do have validators at ~157-177). A plugin author who typos a key is never warned at load. Effect via base.py:159 instance_id_for: an all-typo list makes identity=='' -> returns None -> falls back to full-config hash (tolerable). But a PARTIAL typo (e.g. instance_identity=['host','typo_port']) yields identity 'host|' for EVERY instance, so two instances with the same host but different ports hash to the SAME id and collide.

(b) backend/app/plugins/utils/instance_manager.py:267 collision-resolution branch appends '-{int(time.time()*1000)%100000}' (wraps every 100s) then goes straight to register_plugin() (~275) with NO re-query that the suffixed id is free; if it also exists, register raises 'already registered', caught ~293-299, which silently ENABLES the existing instance instead of creating a new one. Practically hard to hit (needs a prior base-id collision) but a latent uniqueness defect.
design: Both PARTIALLY REAL (high conf) per refuter. Refuter corrected the original scout claim that an all-typo identity collapses all instances to one id — it actually returns None and falls back to config-hash; the real collision is the partial-typo case.
acceptance_criteria: (a) add a PluginMetadata validator that every instance_identity entry exists in instance_config_schema (fail plugin load otherwise). (b) re-check the suffixed id for existence (or use a uuid/counter) before register_plugin. Tests for both.
close_reason: (a) model_validator on PluginMetadata rejects instance_identity keys not in instance/common config schema (fails load). (b) instance_manager re-checks the suffixed id in a while-loop until free. Tests added for (a).

title: InstanceModal drops a legitimate 0 for numeric fields (latent)
description:
frontend/src/components/settings/specialized/InstanceModal.vue lines 438 & 499 save numeric fields with: config[key] = Number(value) || schema.default || 0. Number(0) is falsy, so a user-entered 0 is silently replaced by schema.default (or 0). 

Currently LATENT: no shipped plugin has a field with both a non-zero default AND a valid range including 0, so there is no user-visible symptom today. It bites any future/external plugin with default>0 and min<=0 — e.g. a refresh-interval field with default=60 and min=0 could never be set to 0 (off) from the modal.

Adversarial refuter DROPPED two sibling claims as false positives: (b) PluginFieldRenderer number input emitting a string is fine because backend base.py normalize_config coerces via to_int/to_float; (c) the select-scan disabled placeholder renders correctly as selected in browsers.
design: Filed pending the InstanceModal-values refuter's final verdict; (a) is a clear falsy-0 bug independent of that. If refuter downgrades (b) because normalize_config coerces by type, trim this bead to (a) only.
acceptance_criteria: Preserve 0: use value != null && value !== '' ? Number(value) : (schema.default ?? 0) at both sites. Add a test with a numeric field whose default>0 and min=0, enter 0, assert 0 persists.
close_reason: Preserve 0: value !== '' ? Number(value) : (schema.default ?? 0) at both save sites.

title: Prevent prettier/format debt from reaching develop (guard against tree-wide CI red)
description:
PROBLEM: several develop commits landed without running prettier, so CI's 'prettier --check src/**' and the pre-commit prettier hook failed across the WHOLE tree — turning develop's own CI red and every branch off it red regardless of its diff. Fixed reactively in PR #74 (prettier --write of 8 debt files), then rebased #72/#73.

WHY IT SLIPPED: .pre-commit-config.yaml already has a prettier hook, but it only runs for devs who have 'pre-commit install' set up locally; nothing enforces formatting before push otherwise, and the frontend CI runs eslint + prettier as separate steps (so a green local 'npm run lint' + build can still hit red prettier in CI — exactly what happened here).

OPTIONS (pick one): (a) add a 'format:check' npm script (prettier --check) and document/CI-surface it alongside lint so contributors run it locally; (b) add a husky/simple pre-push hook running prettier --check; (c) add a lint-staged config so staged files auto-format on commit; (d) at minimum, make the local pre-push story obvious in CONTRIBUTING/QUICKSTART. Goal: a formatting miss is caught before it lands on develop, not after it's reddened every open PR.

Related: PR #74 (chore/prettier-format-debt).

title: App-wide: number inputs show native spinner chrome (no shared styled pattern)
description: The px spinner-hiding fix for the clock-bar size inputs (ClockBarFontSizePicker, PR #73) was scoped to .font-size-input. The same native up/down spinner arrows appear on every other type="number" in the app — e.g. SettingItem.vue — because nothing hides them globally (grep for -webkit-inner-spin-button returns nothing). Consider a shared styled number-input pattern (or fold into the ui/ primitives, cf. NumberStepper) so numeric fields are consistent. Low priority; cosmetic.
close_reason: Global input[type=number] spinner-strip added to base.css accessibility baseline; covers SettingItem, PluginFieldRenderer, and clock-bar pickers. Build + prettier green.

title: Design: general two-key chord bindings for keyboard setup
description: Explore letting keyboard bindings be two-key chords (any+any, e.g. 1+7) rather than single keys, so more actions are bindable and the reboot combo could unify as a chord. NOT modifier/Ctrl combos (remotes lack them; browser intercepts). Cost: representation change (KeyboardMappingDB key_code -> normalized combo string like KEY_1+KEY_7), chord capture mode in useKeyCapture, held-set detection + single-vs-combo ambiguity rules in KeyboardHandler.vue. Reboot combo stays special for its hold-N-seconds semantics. Deferred: user is only exploring (no concrete pressure). Write a design spec before building.

title: Global 'Corner style' setting: user-configurable radius scale
description:
Add a global, user-configurable corner-roundness control, mirroring the Settings UI size pattern. Purely cosmetic personalization axis.

MECHANISM: a --radius-scale multiplier baked into the existing radius tokens in frontend/src/styles/theme.css, e.g.
  --radius-xs: calc(6px * var(--radius-scale));  (and sm/md/lg/xl/2xl)
  --radius-pill stays FIXED (999px) — a pill is a pill.
Default --radius-scale = 1 => no-op (baseline unchanged). Discrete PRESETS (not a slider — arbitrary values look broken): e.g. Sharp 0 / Subtle 0.5 / Default 1 / Round 1.6. Stored as a string preset key 'cornerStyle' via /api/config (mirror uiSize plumbing: configRegistry.js + config.js + useConfigForm.js + backend config.py). Preset->factor map in a styles/ module like uiScale.js. Apply via a composable mirroring useUiScale (set --radius-scale on <html>, localStorage boot cache + config sync). UI: SegmentedControl in Settings -> Appearance next to 'Settings UI size'.

BLOCKED BY radius-token adoption — otherwise the knob rounds some elements and not others (whack-a-mole). Must land AFTER:
  - calvin-bvw (region editor adopts --radius-*)
  - calvin-0wr (service regions adopt --radius-*)
Also sweep any remaining hardcoded radii app-wide onto tokens before shipping (grep 'border-radius:.*px' outside theme.css).

OPEN DESIGN Q: standalone global control (recommended, parallels UI size, direct user control) vs. folding radius into the theme layer (each theme defines roundness; keeps appearance model unified). Decide before building.

title: Per-region calendar display overrides in the tune popover (week numbers, event density)
description:
Extend the calendar tune button (RegionViewOptions / CalendarViewOptions, from calvin-bc5) to carry per-region DISPLAY settings as overrides of the global defaults. Design agreed with user 2026-07-03.

SCOPE — settings to move (as per-region overrides):
- Week numbers (global: config.showWeekNumbers)
- Event density / max visible events (global: config.maxVisibleEvents)
DO NOT move: weekStartDay, weekendDays (locale/personal — stay global in Settings), showRedDays (deferred placeholder; isRedDay() returns false).

MODEL — per-region override of a global default (tri-state), NOT a flat move:
- Global Settings keeps the baseline value (unchanged).
- The region 'view' object gains OPTIONAL fields. Absent = inherit the global value, so there is NO data migration for existing regions.
  - CalendarView reads: showWeekNumbers -> props.view?.weekNumbers ?? configStore.showWeekNumbers
  - and maxVisible -> props.view?.maxVisibleEvents ?? configStore.maxVisibleEvents
- Week numbers UI = tri-state segmented control (Default / On / Off). 'Default' persists as undefined/null (or a 'default' sentinel) so it keeps tracking the global.
- Event density UI = a stepper like the existing Weeks/Days stepper, but with a 'Default' affordance (e.g. a Default chip that clears the override back to inherit). Clamp 1–20 to match config setMaxVisibleEvents.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
- Shape/clamp: extend DEFAULT_CALENDAR_VIEW + clampCalendarView in frontend/src/utils/layout.js. Keep new fields optional; clamp only when present (preserve undefined = inherit). Watch the reactive-proxy JSON-clone in setRegionView (see commit 6bd05e7).
- Persist via configStore.updateRegionView(regionId, patch) (same path the tune popover already uses). Setting back to Default should delete the key (patch with undefined) or store a 'default' sentinel — pick one and handle in clamp.
- CalendarView.vue: replace the three global reads (showWeekNumbers, maxVisibleEvents; getVisibleEvents/getOverflowCount use maxVisibleEvents) with view-aware computeds that fall back to global.
- CalendarViewOptions.vue: add the two rows. Consider a small tri-state segmented component (Default/On/Off) — may be reusable; check if one exists before writing a new one.
- Tests: extend CalendarViewOptions.spec + CalendarViewMonth/Rolling or a new spec — assert inherit-from-global when unset, override when set, and that 'Default' clears back to inherit.

Optional follow-on: this same override pattern is what service regions would use via calvin-39g (RegionViewOptions reuse).

STATUS 2026-07-03: Implemented on feat/per-region-calendar-display (commit 09a0313, pushed). Week numbers = compact tri-state Default/On/Off; events/day = stepper + Default reset chip (month only). clampCalendarView keeps weekNumbers (bool) + maxVisibleEvents (1-20) as optional fields, omitted when absent (inherit, no migration). CalendarView reads view ?? global. 834 frontend unit tests pass; lint+prettier clean; verified visually light+dark. PENDING: PR/merge to develop.

title: Display-agent: cap fetch_config response size (unbounded json.load)
description: Security-lens finding (dd9.9 review): fetch_config in deploy/kiosk-agent/calvin_display_agent.py does json.load(r) with no size cap. A hostile/broken LAN backend answering /api/kiosks/<id>/config could return a multi-GB body and OOM the agent (self-recovering via systemd restart). HTTP_TIMEOUT bounds time, not memory. Low priority: unauthenticated-LAN is the pre-existing trust boundary and the failure mode is a restart, not RCE.

title: calendar store: updateSource doesn't refresh calendar_sources cache (stale after offline reboot)

The localStorage cache (1h TTL) keeps pre-edit data. If the kiosk reloads while offline within the hour, fetchSources() serves the stale cached sources and the user's just-saved color/show_time reverts. Plausible on an RPi (settings change then reboot + brief network loss).
design: PARTIALLY REAL, low sev (high conf). Refuter note: the original finding also cited updateRegionView(~354) — that function does NOT exist in calendar.js (phantom). Sibling webServices post-write refetch is self-healing (drops); this one persists across reload because there is no refetch.
acceptance_criteria: After a successful updateSource, setCachedData('calendar_sources', {sources: sources.value}) (or clearCachedData). One-liner; add a test.
close_reason: updateSource now setCachedData('calendar_sources', {sources}). Test added.

title: Schema renderers use array-index v-for keys (ItemList, CardGrid) — transition artifacts on refresh
description: Built-in renderers key v-for by array index over live plugin-data arrays; on a refresh that adds/removes/reorders items, Vue's keyed diff plays enter/leave transitions on the wrong rows and can briefly flicker (final DOM state is still correct — not persistent data corruption). Most impactful where items shift: frontend/src/components/plugins/renderers/ItemList.vue:4 (feeds where new items prepend) and CardGrid.vue:3/7 (cards/inner items that reorder). StatusRenderer.vue (4,19,33) and MetricDashboard.vue (4) are near-harmless (fixed-schema item sets). WeatherForecast.vue already uses a stable key (dateFor(day)||index).
design: PARTIALLY REAL (high conf). Display-only components (no per-item input/focus state), so impact is transition/flicker, not wrong data — hence P4.
acceptance_criteria: Use a stable key where available: timestampFor(item)/labelFor(item) for ItemList, cardTitle(card) for CardGrid outer loop. StatusRenderer/MetricDashboard optional.
close_reason: ItemList/CardGrid use content-based keys (timestamp|label|value / cardTitle) with index fallback.
